question: Should generic tool progress become a public `ReplyPayload` plugin-SDK contract, or remain an internal owner-specific signal?
rationale: The PR adds permanent externally consumable semantics to an already large SDK surface, and tests cannot determine whether maintainers want third-party plugins to depend on this classification.

options.title: Approve generic progress intent
options.body: Keep the additive marker and predicate as a narrow transient-progress contract, document their semantics, and require final-head Slack proof.

options.title: Keep the signal internal
options.body: Move the classification behind an internal or injected owner boundary until another plugin consumer demonstrates a generic SDK need.

recommendation.title: Approve generic progress intent
recommendation.body: Keep the additive marker and predicate as a narrow transient-progress contract, document their semantics, and require final-head Slack proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history connects this person to both the Slack native-data architecture and adjacent Codex app-server behavior affected by the decision.
